source_units.raw_tex:
Let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, which equipped with standard inner product $\langle \cdot,\cdot \rangle$ and norm $\|\cdot \|$, respectively. For any $x,y\in \mathbb{R}^n$, $\|(x,y)\|:=\sqrt{\|x\|^2+\|y\|^2}$. Given a nonempty set $C\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the distance from $z\in \mathbb{R}^n$, the \emph{distance} from $z$ to $C$ is defined as
$\dist(z,C):=\inf_{w\in C}\|w-z\|$. Let $h: \mathbb{R}^n\rightarrow {\mathbb{R}}\cup \{+\infty\}$ be a mapping, the \emph{domain} of $h$ is defined by $\dom h:=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:h(x)<+\infty\}$. The function $h$ is said to be \emph{proper} if $\dom h \neq\varnothing$ and \emph{lower semicontinuous} if $h(x)\leq \liminf_{z\rightarrow x}h(z)$ for any $x\in \mathbb{R}^n$.
